nodes.label: Inert skill catalog (activate-by-copy)
nodes.summary: The master skill DB at ~/ai-os/skills/ never auto-loads. A skill runs only once copied (not symlinked, since 2026-07-17) into a project's .claude/skills/ or .agents/skills/. Copies do not follow DB edits, so drift must be re-checked.

nodes.label: Claude/Codex subtree split, never merged
nodes.summary: Skills are filed under claude/ or codex/ by tool origin and are never merged even when byte-identical. A skill that exists for both tools gets one entry under each so each tool's set stays independently editable.

nodes.label: Save-to-both on skill creation
nodes.summary: Creating a skill writes unconditionally to both the current project's .claude/skills/ (or .agents/skills/) and the master DB, project-scoped by default and never auto-promoted to global.

nodes.label: Vendor skills: live symlink + frozen snapshot
nodes.summary: A vendor or plugin skill gets a live symlink under claude/<name>/ reflecting the installed version plus a frozen copy under _snapshots/ for point-in-time reference. Snapshots refresh manually, never on a schedule.

nodes.label: Generated one-line skill index
nodes.summary: skills/INDEX.md is machine-generated by system/scripts/gen-skill-index.py, one line per skill grouped by source type across the claude/ and codex/ splits. Hand-editing is forbidden.

nodes.label: Project forks of catalog skills
nodes.summary: 23 Claude and 28 Codex skills exist as divergent project-local versions (all under the lsatu project) that have drifted from the catalog copy. The index tracks them as a separate 'project fork' class rather than reconciling them.

nodes.label: LLM wiki pattern (raw / wiki / output)
nodes.summary: Three directories with three roles: raw/ holds immutable sources the LLM never modifies, wiki/ is the LLM's maintained workspace, output/ receives generated artifacts. The LLM acts as librarian, compiling sources into an interlinked wiki.

nodes.label: Raw sources are immutable
nodes.summary: Files in raw/ are read-only source material and must never be modified. The same read-only-input discipline appears in writing-shape, where the raw material pile is a quarry the skill may never edit.

nodes.label: Index + append-only log ledger
nodes.summary: Every wiki operation updates wiki/index.md (one line per page, under 120 chars) and appends a dated entry to wiki/log.md. Log entries are never edited after the fact; the index is the navigation surface until the wiki outgrows it.

nodes.label: Ingest a source into wiki pages
nodes.summary: Read the source completely, discuss takeaways, write a source summary page, then create or update every entity and concept page it touches, add wikilinks, update the index, and log it. One source may touch 10-15 pages.

nodes.label: Query the wiki, index first
nodes.summary: Answer questions by reading wiki/index.md, then the relevant pages, synthesizing with wikilink citations. Valuable answers are offered back as new synthesis pages so explorations compound. Search the wiki before ever going back to raw.

nodes.label: Wiki lint / health check
nodes.summary: Scan for contradictions between pages, stale claims superseded by newer sources, orphan pages with no inbound links, and missing cross-references. Run after every 10 ingests, monthly at minimum, and before any major synthesis.

nodes.label: Second-brain onboarding wizard
nodes.summary: A five-step one-question-at-a-time wizard (vault name, location, domain, agent configs, optional CLI tools) that scaffolds a new Obsidian vault, generates per-agent config files, installs tooling, and logs the setup.

nodes.label: One schema, many agent configs
nodes.summary: wiki-schema.md is the single source of truth; the Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini config templates are byte-identical apart from output filename and location, each injecting {{WIKI_SCHEMA}} from the same file.

nodes.label: Per-runtime agent config file
nodes.summary: Each runtime reads its own root instruction file: CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex, .cursor/rules/second-brain.mdc for Cursor, GEMINI.md for Gemini CLI. Auto-detect the running agent, then offer configs for the others.

nodes.label: Optional local CLI augmentation
nodes.summary: Three optional npm-installed CLIs extend vault work: summarize for link/file/media extraction, qmd for on-device hybrid BM25/vector search once the wiki passes ~100 pages, agent-browser for web research when built-in fetch fails.

nodes.label: Obsidian Web Clipper intake
nodes.summary: The required browser extension that saves web articles as clean markdown straight into the vault's raw/ directory. This is the primary way source material enters the vault without manual copy-paste.

nodes.label: Context window is precious
nodes.summary: Every line of a persistent instruction file must earn its place. Conciseness is scored explicitly, verbose explanations and generic best practices are rejected, and dense beats verbose.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md audit and improve
nodes.summary: Discover every CLAUDE.md variant in a repo, score each against a six-criterion 100-point rubric, emit a quality report before touching anything, then apply approved targeted diffs.

nodes.label: Scored rubric before intervention
nodes.summary: Assess against weighted numeric criteria and publish the scoreboard before proposing changes. CLAUDE.md scoring runs six criteria to 100 with letter grades; the same report-then-fix ordering is treated as mandatory.

nodes.label: Documentation staleness / drift
nodes.summary: Instruction files rot: commands that no longer run, references to deleted files, outdated tech versions, uncustomized template copy-paste, duplicate info across multiple files. Currency is scored and cross-checked against the real codebase.

nodes.label: Instruction-file templates by project type
nodes.summary: Reusable CLAUDE.md skeletons for minimal root, comprehensive root, package/module, and monorepo root, plus section templates for commands, architecture, key files, style, environment, testing, gotchas, and workflow.

nodes.label: Relentless one-question-at-a-time interview
nodes.summary: Walk every branch of the design tree, asking one question at a time and waiting for the answer, always offering a recommended answer, and exploring the codebase instead of asking whenever the code can answer.

nodes.label: Challenge the plan against the glossary
nodes.summary: Call out immediately when a spoken term conflicts with CONTEXT.md, propose precise canonical terms for fuzzy ones, stress-test domain relationships with invented edge-case scenarios, and surface contradictions between what the user says and what the code does.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md as glossary only
nodes.summary: CONTEXT.md is a domain glossary and nothing else: no implementation notes, roadmap, architecture decisions, API details, or scratch-pad thinking. Terms are added only after being resolved with the user, updated inline rather than batched.

nodes.label: ADR three-part necessity test
nodes.summary: Offer an ADR only when all three hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off with credible rejected alternatives. If any is missing, skip it. ADRs are numbered, factual, and never used for reversible detail.

nodes.label: Create docs lazily
nodes.summary: Create CONTEXT.md only when the first term resolves, and docs/adr/ only when the first ADR is needed. A CONTEXT-MAP.md at the root signals a multi-context repo with per-context glossaries and ADR folders.

nodes.label: Cross-model adversarial plan review
nodes.summary: Claude writes the locked plan to PLAN.md and a second model (Codex) attacks it in a read-only sandbox, returning exactly one line of VERDICT: APPROVED or VERDICT: REVISE. Claude revises and re-submits to the same session until convergence or cap.

nodes.label: Bounded loop with MAX_ROUNDS
nodes.summary: The review loop always terminates at MAX_ROUNDS (default 5). Hitting the cap without approval is reported as an honest deadlock with unresolved points and Claude's counter-position, never as faked convergence.

nodes.label: Read-only sandbox enforcement every round
nodes.summary: Codex runs -s read-only on round 1, but resume rejects -s, so rounds 2+ must force -c sandbox_mode="read-only" or Codex inherits config.toml (possibly danger-full-access) and could write files. Flagged as a critical safety line.

nodes.label: codex exec stdin hang under non-TTY drivers
nodes.summary: codex exec reads stdin in addition to the prompt argument, so under a non-interactive driver it blocks forever at ~0% CPU. The < /dev/null redirect is mandatory on both the fresh and resume calls; a 10-minute timeout ceiling makes any remaining stall fail loud.

nodes.label: Same-session resume preserves critic context
nodes.summary: Round 1 captures thread_id from the thread.started JSON line; every later round resumes that same thread so the critic keeps its prior findings in context rather than re-reviewing cold.

nodes.label: Append-only review log as deliverable
nodes.summary: PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md records each round's critique plus Claude's response documenting what changed, what was rejected, and why. The log, not the plan alone, is named the deliverable of the process.

nodes.label: PLAN.md locked plan
nodes.summary: The frozen plan written in the project's canonical terms, with goal, numbered approach, key decisions and tradeoffs with ADR links, risks and open questions, and explicit out-of-scope bounds.

nodes.label: Human sign-off before any code
nodes.summary: No code is written during either act. After convergence the human picks whether Codex builds it, Claude builds it, or work stops. The same gate appears in the CLAUDE.md improver, which never writes until the report is approved.

nodes.label: Decompose into tiniest working commits
nodes.summary: Break an implementation into the smallest possible commits, each leaving the codebase in a working state, per Fowler's advice to always be able to see the program working. Plans are written in plain English without file paths or snippets, which go stale.

nodes.label: Refactor plan filed as a GitHub issue
nodes.summary: A templated issue with problem statement, solution, commit-by-commit plan, decision document, testing decisions, and out-of-scope bounds, produced after an interview and a test-coverage check of the affected area.

nodes.label: Explicit out-of-scope declaration
nodes.summary: Every plan-shaped artifact ends by naming what it will not do. Appears as the Out of Scope section in the locked plan, the refactor issue template, and writing-shape's own boundary list.

nodes.label: Image-first design-to-code workflow
nodes.summary: For visually important web work the model must generate the design reference images itself, deeply analyze them as a specification, then implement. Freeform coding first is forbidden; the image is the design source and the code is the translation layer.

nodes.label: One section, one large image
nodes.summary: Inside Codex, generate one large image per requested section rather than compressing many sections into one board, so text, spacing, buttons, and typography stay analyzable. Never crop a section out of an older larger render; regenerate it fresh.

nodes.label: Forensic design extraction from reference
nodes.summary: Treat the reference as a spec and extract exact text, type scale relationships, spacing and gutters, button shape and hierarchy, palette, radius logic, grid, and repeated motifs before writing any code. Vague vibe-only analysis is rejected.

nodes.label: Design drift during implementation
nodes.summary: The named common failure: strong references become a generic coded result. Guarded by refusing to simplify into default templates, compress generous spacing, flatten typography, or reintroduce removed nesting. The goal is faithful-to, not inspired-by.

nodes.label: Anti-generic AI aesthetic ban list
nodes.summary: Both visual skills enumerate hard bans on the defaults that read as AI-generated: purple/blue gradients, glassmorphism stacking, centered dark hero cliches, generic card spam, banned fonts (Inter, Roboto, Arial), harsh drop shadows, and filler copy like 'unleash' or 'seamless'.

nodes.label: Combinatorial variance engine
nodes.summary: Before coding, silently roll a coherent combination from enumerated archetypes (vibe/texture, layout, typography, hero architecture, signature components, motion cues) and commit to it, so no two outputs share a layout while all stay premium.

nodes.label: Anti-nested-box vs deliberate double-bezel
nodes.summary: A genuine tension between the two visual skills: image-to-code bans cards-inside-cards and giant rounded wrappers, while high-end-visual-design mandates a deliberate two-layer 'Double-Bezel' outer shell plus inner core with concentric radii for every premium container.

nodes.label: Macro-whitespace and breathing room
nodes.summary: Both visual skills demand doubled section padding (py-24 to py-40), restrained first viewports, and negative space as a design material. Density slop, cramped sections, and overfilled heroes are treated as failures.

nodes.label: Physics-based motion choreography
nodes.summary: All motion simulates mass and spring physics via custom cubic-beziers, never linear or ease-in-out. Covers hamburger morph, staggered mask reveals, magnetic button hover with nested icon translation, and heavy scroll fade-ups.

nodes.label: GPU performance guardrails
nodes.summary: Animate only transform and opacity, never top/left/width/height. backdrop-blur only on fixed or sticky elements, noise overlays only on fixed pointer-events-none pseudo-elements, IntersectionObserver instead of scroll listeners, disciplined z-index layers.

nodes.label: Mobile collapse of asymmetric layouts
nodes.summary: Every asymmetric archetype must fall back below 768px to single-column w-full with px-4 py-8, dropping rotations and negative-margin overlaps that cause touch-target conflicts, and using min-h-[100dvh] rather than h-screen to avoid iOS Safari viewport jumping.

nodes.label: Pre-output self-verification checklist
nodes.summary: A final enumerated matrix the model runs against its own output before delivering, refining internally if any item fails. Both visual skills close with one (a 21-point clarity check and an 11-point pre-output matrix).

nodes.label: Accessibility tree as source of truth
nodes.summary: The a11y tree, not the DOM, represents what assistive technology sees, so take_snapshot is the reliable check for semantic structure. Visually hiding via opacity behaves differently from display:none or aria-hidden.

nodes.label: Accessibility audit via DevTools MCP
nodes.summary: Eight-pattern audit: Lighthouse baseline, native browser issues, semantics and heading hierarchy, labels and text alternatives, focus and keyboard traps, tap-target sizing, color contrast, and document-level global checks.

nodes.label: Injected JS probe snippets
nodes.summary: Four reusable evaluate_script snippets that measure what the a11y tree cannot: orphaned form inputs, tap-target bounding boxes, an approximate contrast ratio, and document-level lang/title/viewport/reduced-motion state.

nodes.label: Filter large reports before reading them
nodes.summary: Never read a machine report line by line. Use jq or a Node one-liner to extract only failing audits' selectors and snippets, keeping the full JSON out of the context window.

nodes.label: Draft, never send
nodes.summary: Outbound correspondence to students and prospects is always created as a Gmail draft for Joshua to review, never sent. Repeated as the top-line rule of the consultation follow-up skill and its spec guardrails.

nodes.label: Gemini notes attachment as the did-it-happen signal
nodes.summary: A consultation is ready for follow-up only when the calendar event is in the past, carries a 'Notes by Gemini' or Transcript attachment, and no follow-up has been sent since. Missing notes means skip and wait for the next run.

nodes.label: Idempotent outreach (dedupe before drafting)
nodes.summary: Search Gmail for an existing thread before drafting and skip if a follow-up already went out since the call. One follow-up per consultation; if the student already booked and paid, switch to the onboarding note instead of the sales email.

nodes.label: Mirror a real transcript detail
nodes.summary: Pull the student's diagnostic and target score, study platform, exam timeline, and struggles from the meeting transcript, then personalize the recap line with a real detail and pick the template variant from what the notes revealed.

nodes.label: Read voice + template before drafting
nodes.summary: A required first step: read the email-voice principles and the follow-up template, then follow them exactly. Prose only, no em dashes, under about 150 words, fixed greeting and sign-off.

nodes.label: Scheduled sweep over a calendar window
nodes.summary: A daily run that lists calendar events matching a title pattern over a trailing window, filters by readiness, and produces a queue of drafts plus a report naming anything uncertain for human check.

nodes.label: One-time automations, never recurring
nodes.summary: Pre-consultation check-ins are scheduled as one-time automations exactly one hour before each approved consultation. Recurring or daily automations are forbidden, and temporary setup automations must be disabled afterward.

nodes.label: List candidates, wait for approval
nodes.summary: Search the calendar, list the consultations found, and wait for explicit approval before creating any automation. Never assume which consultations should receive email; if there are none, do nothing.

nodes.label: Reply in the existing thread
nodes.summary: Whenever a thread with the recipient already exists, reply into it rather than starting a new one. Shared by the follow-up drafter and the pre-consultation check-in, and supported natively by the gws reply/forward helpers.

nodes.label: gws CLI as the Google surface
nodes.summary: All 42 gws skills wrap the single gws binary and open with the same prerequisite: read gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules, regenerating it with gws generate-skills if missing.

nodes.label: Hub skill plus per-verb helper skills
nodes.summary: Each gws service has one hub skill listing API resources and linking out to thin per-verb helpers (+send, +read, +forward, +triage, +watch). The hub covers discovery; helpers cover the common flag-level operation.

nodes.label: Inspect the schema before calling the API
nodes.summary: Before invoking any gws API method, browse with --help and run gws schema <resource>.<method> to learn required params, types, and defaults, then build --params and --json from that output rather than guessing.

nodes.label: Dry-run and draft escape hatches
nodes.summary: Mutating gws commands expose --dry-run to show the request without executing and --draft to save instead of send, giving the same review-before-effect posture the drafting skills enforce at the workflow level.

nodes.label: Inbound/outbound content sanitization
nodes.summary: Model Armor templates filter user-generated content at two boundaries: +sanitize-prompt for inbound user-to-model text and +sanitize-response for outbound model-to-user text.

nodes.label: Always-violate rule list
nodes.summary: Twelve never-break LSAT U platform rules kept at the front door for fast access: flags not roles, admin displays as Joshua, no bottom dock, drill always dark, 1:1 messaging only, zero-layout-shift highlighting, SVG not Canvas, Postgres-side provisioning, deterministic channel names, mutations never swallow errors, Causation Station as template, repo-native topic modules.

nodes.label: When-in-doubt binary defaults
nodes.summary: Each architectural rule is restated as a one-word binary answer (flag, Foyer, dark, library, rethrow, repo-native, deterministic, Postgres, SVG, inherit) so a decision needs no re-derivation mid-build.

nodes.label: Indexed front door, canonical body elsewhere
nodes.summary: A skill that carries only fast-access daily rules plus explicit pointers to deeper canonical sources, deliberately not duplicating them. The routing skill's own rules drift and live locally; the pointers stay stable.

nodes.label: Explicit source authority ordering
nodes.summary: Sources are ranked highest to lowest (live repo, audit bundle, vault CLAUDE.md, memory) and on contradiction the lower-authority source is fixed, never the higher. Code is ground truth when documentation drifts.

nodes.label: Pick from the library before building custom
nodes.summary: Choose from the indexed 27-component library first; custom work is warranted only when the existing library cannot teach the topic mechanic. Mirrors the catalog-wide 'search before creating' posture.

nodes.label: Lint-gated scaffolding loop
nodes.summary: Parse the plan, mkdir the directory tree, write stub readmes, run the project linter, and iterate until it passes before committing. The linter's rules are the actual spec for what a valid exercise looks like.

nodes.label: Numeric-prefix directory ordering
nodes.summary: Sections are XX-name and exercises XX.YY-name in dash-case, so the filesystem carries curriculum order. Renumbering uses git mv rather than mv so history survives, then re-lints.

nodes.label: Problem / solution / explainer variants
nodes.summary: Each exercise carries at least one of problem/ (student workspace with TODOs), solution/ (reference implementation), or explainer/ (conceptual, no TODOs), each needing a non-empty readme. Stubs default to explainer.

nodes.label: Conversational article shaping
nodes.summary: Turn a pile of raw material into an article by drafting 2-3 candidate openings that imply different theses, forcing a pick, then growing the piece one agreed block at a time, appending to the article file as it goes.

nodes.label: Argue format tradeoffs out loud
nodes.summary: Each beat's rendering is a deliberate defensible choice weighed with the user: prose vs list, inline vs callout, table vs repeated structure, quote vs paraphrase, code block vs inline code.

nodes.label: Re-read from disk before every write
nodes.summary: The user edits the artifact between turns, so re-read the file from disk before writing and never overwrite blindly. Rewrites edit the specific paragraph in place and leave the rest alone.

nodes.label: Name the gap rather than inventing
nodes.summary: When the source pile lacks something the output needs, say so explicitly and make the user fill it or cut the section, instead of quietly fabricating material.

nodes.label: Recover original intent before resolving
nodes.summary: For each conflicting hunk, read commit messages, PRs, and original issues to understand deeply why each change was made, then preserve both intents where possible and note the trade-off where incompatible.

nodes.label: Always resolve, never invent behaviour
nodes.summary: A merge conflict must always be resolved and never --abort'ed, and the resolution must not introduce new behaviour that was in neither side.

nodes.label: Discover and run the project's own checks
nodes.summary: After a structural change, find the project's automated checks (typecheck, then tests, then format) and run them, fixing whatever the change broke before finishing. The lint-gated scaffolder applies the same gate.

nodes.label: Codex plugin scaffolding
nodes.summary: Script-driven creation of a Codex plugin directory with a required .codex-plugin/plugin.json, normalized lower-case hyphen-case name, optional companion folders (skills, hooks, scripts, assets, .mcp.json, .app.json), and a personal-marketplace entry by default.

nodes.label: Plugin manifest schema contract
nodes.summary: Manifests need real values for name, version (strict semver), description, author.name, and required interface fields. Absolute https URLs, real asset files, no unsupported fields such as hooks, and apps/mcpServers only when the companion file exists.

nodes.label: Marketplace entry policy defaults
nodes.summary: Every generated entry writes policy.installation (default AVAILABLE), policy.authentication (default ON_INSTALL), and category even when default. policy.products is an override omitted unless asked. Entries are appended, and array order is Codex's render order.

nodes.label: Validate before handing back
nodes.summary: Run scripts/validate_plugin.py against the plugin path before returning it. The validator mirrors the workspace ingestion schema and adds a preflight that rejects leftover [TODO: ...] placeholders.

nodes.label: Cachebuster + reinstall update loop
nodes.summary: To update a local plugin, stamp a single Codex cachebuster suffix (<base-version>+codex.<token>, replacing rather than appending), read the marketplace name, reinstall with codex plugin add, then start a new thread to pick up new skills and tools.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit generated config
nodes.summary: Marketplace manipulation happens through scripts and CLI commands, never by hand-editing marketplace.json or config.toml. Mirrors the generated skill index that must not be hand-edited.

nodes.label: Implicit personal vs explicit marketplace discovery
nodes.summary: The default personal marketplace at ~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json is discovered implicitly and must NOT be registered with codex plugin marketplace add. Any other path is not discovered and must be installed first or reinstall instructions will fail.

nodes.label: Local-DB channel with allowlist gating
nodes.summary: iMessage has no token: it reads ~/Library/Messages/chat.db directly, gated by macOS Full Disk Access. Inbound senders are gated by access.json, re-read on every message so policy changes take effect without restart.

nodes.label: Prefer allowlist over pairing
nodes.summary: Because the DB is personal and the handles are already known, pairing has no upside and a clear downside: every contact who texts the Mac gets an unsolicited auto-reply. The skill actively pushes back when a user asks for pairing.

nodes.label: Report status, then one concrete next step
nodes.summary: Read the actual state, present it completely, and end with a single concrete next action conditioned on that state rather than a menu of possibilities.

nodes.label: Third-party attribution and license notices
nodes.summary: Skills adapted from external work carry a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md naming the upstream author and license, and separate the borrowed part from original additions. Reference bundles are kept in a distinct tree marked as not-authored-here.
